data.long_meaning: Ekanam means 'The One Supreme Power' in Hindu tradition. The name Ekanam carries the meaning “One Supreme Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekanam usually hope their child will grow to embody one supreme power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ekanam holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is a reminder of the monistic belief of Advaita Vedanta, which asserts that there is only one ultimate reality or consciousness. The name emphasizes the unity and non-dualistic nature of the universe, and encourages those who bear it to strive towards achieving oneness with the Divine. Ekanam is also an auspicious name and is believed to bring blessings of knowledge, wisdom, and divine protection.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ekanam holds immense importance as it represents the ultimate truth and reality of the universe, which is God or the Supreme consciousness. The name is a constant reminder to people who bear it of the unity and oneness of all things in the universe and encourages them to focus their attention inward towards the self and the Divine. The name also holds the power to uplift the mind, providing inner peace and strength, and inspiring one to lead a virtuous and disciplined life, dedicated to the pursuit of spiritual growth and awareness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ekanam signifies the supreme oneness with the Divine. It represents the unity of the individual soul with the universal consciousness, symbolizing the ultimate goal of spiritual pursuits in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Ekanam was an important Jaina monk, teacher and philosopher who lived during the 5th and 6th centuries CE in India. He was a key figure in the development of the Digambara sect of Jainism. Ekanam is best known for his work 'Tattvartha Sutra' which is considered a fundamental text in the Digambara tradition.
historical_references.context: Jainism, Digambara sect, philosopher, teacher, author of Tattvartha Sutra

historical_references.reference: Ekanam is also known as Haribhadra Suri. He was a prominent Jain monk and scholar who lived during the 10th and 11th centuries CE in India. He is credited with writing influential commentaries on the 'Agama Sastra' and the 'Nyaya Sutra' which significantly contributed to the understanding and expansion of Jain philosophy.
historical_references.context: Jainism, scholar, author of influential commentaries on Agama Sastra and Nyaya Sutra
